decompileLimit: Il2CppInterop stubs carry signatures, fields and CallerCount/RVA metadata but no bodies. Anything needing a body is marked unverified.

types.role: one player's authoritative ammunition pool, reached through PlayerBackpack.AmmoStorage

fields.name: StandardAmmo / SpecialAmmo / ClassAmmo / ResourcePackAmmo / ConsumableAmmo
fields.note: one entry per AmmoType, plus the per-slot table

fields.name: NeedsSync
fields.usedFor: the game's own marker that this storage has pending synchronised state; recorded, not published

members.name: GetClipBulletsFromPack
members.usedFor: the one method whose name states it pulls rounds out of the pack into a clip; the adapter watches its post-body readback for a transfer, because the body itself cannot say how many rounds moved

members.name: PickupAmmo
members.usedFor: refilled: the pool grew because ammunition was picked up

members.name: FillAllClips
members.usedFor: refilled: the pool filled every clip at once

members.name: Reset
members.usedFor: refilled with the reset source when the pool grew; a reset that empties the pool publishes nothing, because a refill is a gain

members.name: SetStorageData
members.usedFor: the synchronised arrival of another machine's pool; a gain observed here is a refilled with the sync source

members.name: GetAmmoTypeFromSlot
members.usedFor: the slot-to-pool mapping, read from the game rather than reimplemented

types.finding: A slot's pool exposes the rounds in the pack and the clip size, but NOT the rounds currently in the magazine: the clip lives on the wielded ItemEquippable (GetCurrentClip). A transfer therefore has to be measured across both objects, which is what the adapter does.
types.usedFor: refilled reads BulletsInPack before and after a pool write; a gain is the refill amount.

types.role: one player's slots and the pool they draw from

fields.name: Slots
fields.usedFor: the slot table every stack and pickup readback walks

fields.name: OnStorageUpdatedCallback
fields.note: declared and written by the game; one consumer in this build (PlaceNavMarkerOnGO). Not treated as an event source here: the pool write hooks are the readback points, so one change cannot be billed twice.

members.name: CreateAndStoreBackpackItem
members.usedFor: picked_up: the slot now holds an item

members.name: TryClearSlot
members.usedFor: dropped: the slot no longer holds the item that was there

members.name: CountPocketItem
members.usedFor: stack_changed: the count the game answers for one item id, which is the group the pocket slots holding that id form

members.name: IsDeployed
members.note: a deployed slot stays occupied; the existing adapter already tags it deployed, and this family publishes no drop for it

types.finding: A slot entry holds no stack count, so the slot table alone can only say whether an item is there. The count the stack row publishes is the backpack's own pocket count for that item id, which is what groups the pocket slots holding the same id into one stack; a slot whose block is not carried in a pocket has no count at all and publishes no count row.
types.unverified: Whether any item in this build carries a stack greater than one inside a single slot; the count is the game's own per-id answer over the pocket table either way, so a single slot holding five rounds of one id reads as five.

types.role: the ammunition pack that lies in the level
callEdges: w1-native-hooks.json: resource-pack-sync.picks-up reaches ItemInLevel.OnPickedUp (0x147B530), which reaches TryClearSlot for the occupying item (level-pickup.drops-occupied-slot)
w1-native-hooks.json: consumable-sync.picks-up is the same edge for ConsumablePickup_Core
types.finding: Picking a pack up is observed through the slot table: the item that occupied the target slot leaves it and the pack's contents arrive in the pool. The pack's own component is not hooked, because the slot and pool readbacks already carry the fact and a third path would let one pickup be published twice. The pack holding a capacity in m_capacityDebug is NOT read: the amount that actually arrived is what the pool reports.
types.unverified: Which AmmoType a pack feeds is not stated by any member this decompile exposes; the adapter reports the pool that actually grew.

types.role: the use side of the equipment family

members.name: TryStartAnimationSequenceCoroutine
members.usedFor: use_started: the one sequence entry every use animation goes through, including the reload sequence, which is why IsReloading is read first. Private on this build; Harmony patches it by name, and it is not part of any public surface this package calls directly.

members.name: IsReloading
members.usedFor: the discriminator that keeps a reload from being published as a use_started

members.name: OnBatteryLevelChange
members.usedFor: energy_changed for a tool whose charge is a battery level

members.name: GetCurrentClip / SetCurrentClip / GetMaxClip
members.usedFor: energy_changed for a tool whose charge is its clip (the pressure and recharge family), and the clip readback reload_transferred compares against

members.name: ConsumesBattery
members.note: overridden by ImpactHammer in this build; the base returns a value this decompile cannot read

types.role: the use gate this family reports a refusal from

members.name: CanReloadCurrent
members.usedFor: use_failed: a reload the player asked for and the game refused

members.name: TriggerReload
members.usedFor: the ask that the gate above answers

types.role: the tool whose charge is pressure rather than ammunition

members.name: GetCurrentClip
members.usedFor: the charge readback; the tool's charge is what its clip getter answers

types.finding: A tool's charge is observable through the same GetCurrentClip member a magazine weapon answers with, so energy_changed needs no second readback path. GlueGun.CanReload is overridden, which is evidence that the reload gate is per-family and must be asked rather than assumed.

energyScope.rule: energy_changed is published from ItemEquippable.OnBatteryLevelChange when the item consumes a battery, and otherwise from a change of the item's own clip readback while the player's ammunition pool for that slot did not move. A change that the pool explains is the ammunition family's and is not republished here.
energyScope.why: The two tool shapes this build shows are a battery level (OnBatteryLevelChange, overridden by ImpactHammer) and a charge held as the item's clip (GlueGun's pressure). Both are the item's own energy; a pool movement is ammunition and belongs to ammo_changed and refilled.

droppedDefinition.definition: the item left the backpack slot it occupied
droppedDefinition.whyItCannotBeNarrowed: TryClearSlot returns a bool and carries no reason (w1-native-hooks.json already records that its readback does not distinguish causes). Its callers in this build include Throw, the mine's local-slot removal, a level pickup dropping the occupying item, RemoveItem and Reset, and its body destroys the instance, while SetDeployed marks a placed sentry or mine rather than clearing it. A 'player chose to drop it' reading is not supported by any member this decompile exposes.
droppedDefinition.consequence: The position port is omitted, because a slot clear does not report where the item went and the instance is usually already destroyed by the time the post-body readback runs. A position is published only when the run's owner adapter still holds a world instance for the item and can read a finite transform from it; the port is optional in the row for exactly this reason.
droppedDefinition.notPublished: A deployed marker (SetDeployed true) never produces a dropped: the item is still the slot's own equipment and the existing adapter already tags it deployed.

useFailedScope.rule: use_failed is a use the player asked for that the native gate refused. Its outcome is execution_outcome and its reason is the gate's own name.
covered: PlayerInventoryBase.TriggerReload ran and PlayerInventoryBase.CanReloadCurrent returned false: outcome rejected, reason 'not-reloadable'.
notCoveredAndWhy: A shot refused for an empty magazine is forge.trigger.combat.dry_fire and is never published here; Weapon.m_wasOutOfAmmo is dry_fire's readback.
A tool or consumable refused for a depleted battery: no gate method is exposed for it (ConsumesBattery has no body in this decompile), so it is reported as a gap rather than published from a guess.
PlayerBackpack.TryClearSlot returning false as a refused use: the existing evidence already records that its return value is not a reason, and a false return there is also what a teardown looks like.
useFailedScope.division: dry_fire is the ammunition-gate refusal of a firing weapon; use_failed is every other refused use. The two rows never name the same event.

unverified: What PlayerInventoryBase.pSimpleItemSyncData.inCooldown means for a tool; nothing is published from it.
Whether BackpackItem can hold more than one of an item; the stack row is therefore defined over slot occupancy.
Whether ResourcePackPickup feeds a specific AmmoType; the pool that actually grew is what is reported.
Whether TryClearSlot's false return is reachable from a player action; no drop is published from a refusal.
